news.headline: Euronet Worldwide Inc.
news.quote: received a buyout bid from Euronet Worldwide Inc.

touches.claim: Cross-Border Payments (formerly Money Transfer) is weakening: Q3 2026 revenue was $431.0 million, down 5% from $452.4 million, and operating income was $37.3 million, down 37% from $59.3 million.

Leverage is meaningful: total indebtedness was $2,177.3 million at September 30, 2026, and nine-month operating cash flow fell to 252.1 from 381.9 (table in millions) while earnings softened. Credit-facility covenants require EBITDA and leverage ratios to be met.

Cross-Border Payments is the main current threat to results. Quarterly revenues fell 5% to $431.0 million from $452.4 million, and operating income fell 37% to $37.3 million from $59.3 million. Management attributes this to U.S. immigration policy and global economic uncertainty.

Growth funding depends on keeping the balance sheet in order: total indebtedness was $2,177.3 million, down from $2,654.0 million at June 30, and management says it will keep reducing debt to maintain its investment-grade rating. It also repurchased $50 million of stock in the quarter. Reinvestment and buybacks must therefore fit within that debt-reduction commitment.

news.why: Euronet submitted a buyout bid for MoneyGram International, a major money-transfer acquisition attempt that bears directly on its pressured Cross-Border Payments segment and its debt-reduction and leverage commitments.

business_model.claim: Euronet sells payment and transaction processing and distribution solutions to financial institutions, retailers, service providers and individual consumers.
quotes: We offer payment and transaction processing and distribution solutions to financial institutions, retailers, service providers and individual consumers.

business_model.claim: The company reports three segments: Payments Infrastructure (ATMs, POS and processing), epay (prepaid and digital content distribution) and Cross-Border Payments (money transfer). In May the first and third were renamed from EFT Processing and Money Transfer, and the composition did not change.
quotes: In May 2026, the Company changed the name of the EFT Processing Segment to Payments Infrastructure and the name of the Money Transfer Segment to Cross-Border Payments in order to more accurately reflect the products and services provided by these segments.

business_model.claim: Revenue mix for the third quarter was about 38% Payments Infrastructure, 25% epay and 37% Cross-Border Payments. For the nine months it was about 34%, 27% and 39%.
quotes: Revenues in the PI Segment, which represented approximately 38% and 34% of total consolidated revenues for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026

business_model.claim: Payments Infrastructure earns money from fees on its own ATM network (management fees, transaction fees, surcharges, margins on dynamic currency conversion) and from outsourced ATM and card processing. It also earns software license, maintenance and related hardware revenue.
quotes: The primary sources of revenues generated by our ATM network are recurring monthly management fees, transaction-based fees, surcharges, and margins earned on DCC transactions.

business_model.claim: In the third quarter Payments Infrastructure revenue rose to $437.9 million, up 7% from $409.4 million, with active ATMs of 58,420, up 4% from 56,431. Growth came from merchant acquiring, Ren sales and the CoreCard acquisition, partly offset by pressure on discretionary travel spend.
quotes: Constant currency revenue growth was driven by continued growth in merchant acquiring, Ren sales, and the fourth quarter 2025 acquisition of CoreCard, partially offset by continued economic pressures on discretionary travel spend which negatively affects international ATM cash withdrawals.

business_model.claim: Transaction growth in Payments Infrastructure does not translate proportionately into revenue. Transactions processed rose to 15,534 (table in millions) from 11,424 (table in millions) on low-value digital payments, while revenue per transaction fell to $0.08 from $0.10.
quotes: As a result, our revenue growth will not correlate proportionately with the increase in our transaction volume growth.
Revenue per transaction was $0.08 and $0.10 for the year ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited item (annual report description)
business_model.claim: Payments Infrastructure direct costs are mostly operating costs of the ATM estate: site rental, cash delivery and supply, maintenance, insurance, telecommunications, scheme fees and processing-center costs, plus commissions on POS dynamic currency conversion.
quotes: Direct operating costs primarily consist of site rental fees, cash delivery costs, cash supply costs, maintenance, insurance, telecommunications, payment scheme processing fees, data center operations-related personnel, as well as the processing centers’ facility-related costs and other processing center-related expenses and commissions paid to retail merchants, banks and card processors involved with POS DCC transactions.

business_model.claim: epay earns commissions and processing fees on prepaid mobile airtime and digital content distributed through retailers, and its main cost is commissions paid to those retail merchants. Digital media content is now about 77% of epay revenue.
quotes: primarily derived from commissions or processing fees received from mobile phone operators for the processing and distribution of prepaid mobile airtime and commissions earned from the distribution of other electronic content, vouchers, and physical gifts.

Direct operating costs primarily consist of the commissions paid to retail merchants for the distribution and sale of prepaid mobile airtime and other prepaid products, expenses incurred to operate POS terminals and the cost of vouchers sold and physical gifts fulfilled.

business_model.claim: In the third quarter epay revenue was $294.7 million, up 3% from $286.5 million, with transactions of 1,191 million, up 4%. The company attributes growth to higher-value digital content, merchant acquiring and promotional campaigns.
quotes: Constant currency revenue and operating income each increased 5% and adjusted EBITDA increased 6% as a result of continued demand for higher-value digital content, merchant acquiring and promotional campaigns.

business_model.claim: Cross-Border Payments earns transaction fees plus the foreign exchange margin between wholesale purchase and retail sale of currency. Sending and correspondent agents are paid fees that are booked as direct operating costs at the time of sale.
quotes: are primarily derived from transaction fees, as well as the margin earned from purchasing foreign currency at wholesale exchange rates and selling the foreign currency to customers at retail exchange rates.
Sending and correspondent agents each earn fees for cash collection and distribution services, which are recognized as direct operating costs at the time of sale.

business_model.claim: Cross-Border Payments is currently the pressure point. The company says U.S. outbound remittance volumes are lower because of U.S. immigration policy changes and the U.S. remittance tax, while digital transactions keep growing.
quotes: More recently, the U.S. outbound remittance market has experienced lower transaction volumes due to changes in U.S. immigration policies and the implementation of the U.S. remittance tax, which have affected certain remittance corridors.

business_model.claim: In the third quarter Cross-Border Payments revenue was $431.0 million, down 5% from $452.4 million. Operating income was $37.3 million, down 37% from $59.3 million, and digital transactions were 8.1 million, up 34% from 6.1 million.

Nine-month repayments of credit agreements were 6,322.7 against borrowings of 7,007.5, repayment of long-term debt was 700.4, and the statement also shows proceeds from convertible notes of 1,000.0, a capped call of (99.8) and debt issuance costs of (23.5) (table in millions).

financial_health.basis: Availability stated in P6; the link to the current debt is inferred.
financial_health.claim: How debt can be met: the company reports revolving-credit availability of about $1.1 billion, plus unrestricted cash of 955.4 (table in millions) and operating cash flow of 252.1 over nine months. Together these are the stated sources for repaying the current debt of 470.5.
quotes: Availability under the Company's revolving credit facilities was approximately $1.1 billion.

financial_health.basis: Covenants stated in P2 (annual filing); EBITDA figures stated in P6; the sensitivity is inferred.
financial_health.claim: Covenant constraint: the credit facility has two financial covenants, a Consolidated Total Leverage Ratio and a Consolidated Interest Coverage Ratio. Falling EBITDA could therefore limit borrowing headroom. Third-quarter Adjusted EBITDA was $226.1 million versus $244.6 million, and the 2026 outlook is approximately $725 million.
quotes: Our Credit Facility (as defined below) contains two financial covenants that we must meet as defined in the agreement: (1) Consolidated Total Leverage Ratio, and (2) Consolidated Interest Coverage Ratio.

financial_health.basis: Share counts stated in F2 and P6; the link to the notes is stated in the P6 reconciliation label.
financial_health.claim: The convertible notes add dilution but not near-term cash outflow in the evidence. Diluted weighted shares for the third quarter were 45,761,882 versus basic 37,289,653, and the adjusted-EPS reconciliation removes 8,047,923 shares for convertible-note dilution.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the earnings release and the 10-Q income statement.
growth_thesis.claim: Consolidated growth is currently slow: Q3 2026 revenues rose 1% to $1,161.1 million from $1,145.7 million, while operating income fell 12% to $171.6 million from $195.0 million. Any growth thesis therefore rests on the segment drivers below outweighing the Cross-Border Payments decline.
quotes: Revenues of $1,161.1 million, a 1% increase from $1,145.7 million (3% increase on a constant currency1 basis).

growth_thesis.claim: Payments Infrastructure (formerly EFT Processing) is the strongest revenue driver, with Q3 revenues of $437.9 million, up 7% from $409.4 million. Continuing growth requires merchant acquiring, Ren sales and the CoreCard contribution to keep growing faster than the drag from weaker discretionary travel spend and cost inflation.
quotes: Constant currency revenue growth was driven by continued growth in merchant acquiring, Ren sales, and the fourth quarter 2025 acquisition of CoreCard, partially offset by continued economic pressures on discretionary travel spend which negatively affects international ATM cash withdrawals.

growth_thesis.basis: ATM counts are stated in the earnings release; the renewal condition is stated in the 10-K risk factors.
growth_thesis.claim: ATM network expansion supports volume growth: active ATMs were 58,420 at September 30, 2026, a 4% increase from 56,431. Continuing this requires the card acceptance and ATM management agreements to be renewed, since a number of them expire or come up for renewal each year.
quotes: Total of 58,420 active ATMs as of September 30, 2026, a 4% increase from 56,431 as of September 30, 2025.
Our existing contracts generally have terms of five to seven years and a number of them expire or are up for renewal each year.

growth_thesis.basis: Acquisition and its revenue contribution are stated in the filings; the integration condition is stated in the 10-K risk factors.
growth_thesis.claim: The CoreCard acquisition is a source of Payments Infrastructure growth but adds cost: it raised non-cash purchase price amortization by $4.7 million in Q3. It continues to help only if integration succeeds.
quotes: On October 30, 2025, the Company completed the acquisition of 100% of the outstanding equity of CoreCard Corporation.
Successfully integrating acquired businesses, including CoreCard, can be complex and challenging.

growth_thesis.basis: Results are stated in the earnings release; contract risk is stated in the 10-K risk factors.
growth_thesis.claim: The epay segment is a steady driver: Q3 revenues were $294.7 million, up 3% from $286.5 million, with constant currency growth led by higher-value digital content, merchant acquiring and promotional campaigns. It needs continued demand for digital content, and its content provider and retailer contracts have to be renewed on acceptable terms.
quotes: Constant currency revenue and operating income each increased 5% and adjusted EBITDA increased 6% as a result of continued demand for higher-value digital content, merchant acquiring and promotional campaigns.

The cancellation or non-renewal of one or more of our significant content provider or retail contracts, or of a large enough group of our contracts with smaller retailers, could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, and results of operations.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the earnings release; the revenue base for the accelerators is not given.
growth_thesis.claim: The company's named digital accelerators are its stated growth engine: their revenue increased 33% over nine months and represented 26% of year-to-date revenues. This requires continued investment in Ria digital, merchant acquiring and Ren.
quotes: increased 33% for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and represented 26% of year-to-date revenues

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the earnings release; the offset condition is inferred from the total transaction and revenue declines.
growth_thesis.claim: Digital cross-border transactions are growing: Q3 digital transactions were 8.1 million, up 34% from 6.1 million. For the segment to return to growth, digital volume must grow enough to offset declines in retail transactions.
quotes: Total digital transactions of 8.1 million, a 34% increase from 6.1 million.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the earnings release and the 10-Q MD&A; the 'must ease' condition is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: A recovery in the U.S. remittance market is a condition for Cross-Border Payments growth: the segment's Q3 operating income fell 37% to $37.3 million from $59.3 million, and management says pressure from U.S. immigration policy and the remittance tax must ease. Management reports the decline improved slightly from the prior quarter and trends are stabilizing to modestly improving, but it calls the market fragile.
quotes: Pressure persisted primarily in the U.S. market, but the last few months have shown stabilizing to modestly improving trends.

growth_thesis.claim: Management's revised 2026 outlook, lowered from the Investor Day targets, is for approximately $4.375 billion of revenue, approximately $725 million of Adjusted EBITDA and adjusted EPS growth of approximately 10%. It assumes no further adverse changes in exchange rates, interest rates or other factors.
quotes: We now expect approximately $4.375 billion of revenue, approximately $725 million of Adjusted EBITDA and adjusted EPS growth of approximately 10%.

growth_thesis.basis: Share counts and repurchase are stated; the link to per-share growth is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: Per-share growth is supported by buybacks: basic weighted average shares were 37,289,653 in Q3 2026 versus 40,331,347 a year earlier, and $50 million of stock was repurchased in the quarter. Continuing this requires cash generation and leverage low enough to protect the investment-grade rating.
quotes: The Company remains committed to reducing its debt balances in order to maintain its investment-grade credit rating.

growth_thesis.basis: Cash flow and availability are stated; the link to expansion capacity is inferred from the 10-K risk factors.
growth_thesis.claim: Funding capacity is a condition for continued expansion: nine-month operating cash flow was 252.1 versus 381.9 a year earlier (table in millions), and the company had about $1.1 billion available under its revolving credit facilities. ATM cash and acquisitions both draw on capital.
quotes: Availability under the Company's revolving credit facilities was approximately $1.1 billion.

material_events.basis: Stated in the cited 8-K earnings release. The prior Investor Day targets are not given in the evidence, so the size of the cut is not known.
material_events.claim: With its Q3 2026 results the company cut its 2026 outlook from the Investor Day targets to about $4.375 billion revenue, about $725 million Adjusted EBITDA and about 10% adjusted EPS growth, citing Cross-Border Payments pressure.
quotes: We now expect approximately $4.375 billion of revenue, approximately $725 million of Adjusted EBITDA and adjusted EPS growth of approximately 10%.

material_events.basis: Stated in the cash flow statement line item. The event date is inferred only to fall within the nine-month period.

quotes: Proceeds from convertible notes | 1,000.0

material_events.basis: Stated in the 10-K Item 1 and corroborated by the Q3 2026 earnings release.
material_events.claim: The company completed the acquisition of 100% of CoreCard Corporation, which the Q3 2026 release says lifted Payments Infrastructure revenue and added non-cash purchase price amortization.
quotes: On October 30, 2025, the Company completed the acquisition of 100% of the outstanding equity of CoreCard Corporation.

quotes: after the money transfer services company received a buyout bid from Euronet Worldwide Inc.

risks.basis: Stated in the Q3 2026 earnings release and 10-Q MD&A. The causal link is management's own explanation.
risks.claim: Cross-Border Payments (the money transfer business) is shrinking: Q3 2026 revenue fell 5% to $431.0 million and operating income fell 37% to $37.3 million. Management ties this to U.S. immigration policy and economic pressure.
quotes: Constant currency revenue was impacted by continued pressure from U.S. immigration policy and broader global economic uncertainty, partially offset by continued strength in the digital business, with digital transactions growing 34% and continued momentum in our Dandelion cross-border payments platform.

risks.basis: The revision and its exclusions are stated in the release. The risk of a further cut is inferred.
risks.claim: The company has already cut its 2026 outlook to about $4.375 billion of revenue, about $725 million of Adjusted EBITDA and about 10% adjusted EPS growth. The outlook excludes further FX, interest-rate or other changes, so further revisions remain possible.
quotes: This outlook does not include any further changes that may develop in foreign exchange rates, interest rates or other unforeseen factors.

risks.basis: The figures are stated. The risk mechanism is inferred, and the covenant description comes from the 10-K risk factors.
risks.claim: Debt is material: total indebtedness was $2,177.3 million, of which $470.5 of short-term debt and current maturities is due within a year (table in millions). Nine-month operating cash flow fell to $252.1 from $381.9 (table in millions).
quotes: The Company remains committed to reducing its debt balances in order to maintain its investment-grade credit rating.

risks.basis: The figures are stated in the 10-Q statements and the release. The margin-compression mechanism is inferred.
risks.claim: Consolidated operating income fell in Q3 2026 to 171.6 from 195.0 (table in millions) even as revenue rose. Management cites cost inflation, and D&A and SG&A rose.
quotes: Adjusted EBITDA and operating income were impacted by continued cost inflation.

risks.basis: The FX exposure is stated in the 10-Q. The link to the outlook cut is stated in the release. How much comes from FX is not quantified.
risks.claim: About 77% of revenue is in non-U.S. dollar currencies, so exchange-rate moves can significantly affect reported results. Management cites FX conversion rate changes as one reason for the revised outlook.
quotes: any significant changes in foreign currency exchange rates will likely have a significant impact on our results of operations
